name: Megali Idea
summary: The Megali Idea (Great Idea) is the Greek irredentist programme of uniting the Greeks still outside the kingdom, in the Ottoman Empire and elsewhere, in one state centred on Constantinople. It joined a modern constitutional nation with the memory of classical Athens and the Orthodox Byzantine Empire. It guided Greek foreign policy from 1844 until the defeat in Asia Minor in 1922.
scope: The mainstream Greek irredentist programme from Kolettis's 1844 speech to the Venizelist drive at the Paris Peace Conference and the 1919-1922 Asia Minor war. Based on Kolettis's speech in the 1843-44 National Assembly, Venizelos's 1919 memorandum and standard historical accounts. It excludes later Greek or Cypriot nationalism after 1922 and the communist and royalist factions' separate agendas. Economic and social answers are mostly inferred and low confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Pre-1922 Greek nationalism had no health programme; Venizelist liberalism leaned toward modest social reform, but adherents were not defined by it.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Venizelos passed early labour laws, but wage floors were not part of the national project and adherents had no common line.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The idea was about borders, not economics; Venizelist liberals favoured a mixed, capitalist order while Kolettis-era politics was patronage-based.

public-ownership.rationale: Venizelism was bourgeois-liberal and never advocated nationalising industry; inferred from its liberal reform record.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No stated position; war finance and refugee settlement pressed on budgets but the ideology had no distributive doctrine.

unions-good.rationale: Venizelos legalised some labour organisation in 1910s reforms, yet the ideology treated class interests as secondary to the nation.

property-fundamental.rationale: Venizelist liberalism assumed a bourgeois property order; inferred, not stated in the idea itself.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Economic regulation was not part of the idea; adherents divided by party.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; the 19th-century kingdom had almost no welfare state to cut, so no clear position can be inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: Alien to a nationalist-liberal programme; inferred from Venizelism's capitalist orientation.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Anachronistic question; security policy was subordinate to the national struggle but no stance on surveillance is documented.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the conservative, Orthodox-inflected social outlook of Greek nationalism.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed by the idea; adherents had no defined view.

strong-leader.rationale: Kolettis ruled through patronage and Venizelos was a charismatic leader, but the Venizelist cause was constitutional and fought royal overreach, so adherents split.

state-harmful.rationale: The idea is about building a larger Greek state with Constantinople as capital, so calling the state harmful is the opposite of its core aim.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed by the idea; no documented position.

empower-police-military.rationale: Venizelos modernised the army before the Balkan Wars and the idea required military strength to realise it.

decide-locally.rationale: Kolettis and Venizelos built a centralised nation-state aiming to gather all Hellenes under one government in Athens or Constantinople.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal policy was not part of the idea.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred from the Orthodox, conservative social setting in which the idea flourished; not a doctrinal element.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Orthodox-linked social conservatism of its adherents.

abortion-legal.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Orthodox Christian identity that Kolettis treated as binding the nation.

more-religion-public.rationale: Kolettis called religion the guardian of national unity and defined Greeks as those who believe in Christ, giving Orthodoxy a public national role.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Anachronistic; the idea has no position on redress for racial injustice.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from traditional social views of the period.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Kolettis's speech and the idea itself rest on preserving and reuniting Hellenic and Byzantine heritage as the national mission.

gradual-change.rationale: The idea pursued sudden territorial transformation through war and revolt, and Venizelos staged a revolution in 1916, though within established monarchy early on.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Greek nationalism treated co-ethnics as returnees rather than immigrants; no stance on general immigration levels.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Venizelos appealed to the Peace Conference and League principles, but adherents wanted Greek sovereignty, not supranational authority; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed; adherents had no common trade doctrine.

nation-first.rationale: The memorandum asks that Greek national claims be met in the peace settlement and puts national unity ahead of other aims.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Greek claims were framed as liberating oppressed co-nationals, so intervention for kin is accepted, though the statement is broader.

open-borders.rationale: The project was to redraw borders around Greek populations, and Venizelos proposed population movements to homogenise states.

limit-growth.rationale: Anachronistic; the idea assumes expansion of state and population.

revolution-justified.rationale: The idea grew from the 1821 uprising and Greek revolts in Crete and Macedonia; Kolettis invokes the oath of the revolution as the nation's founding act.

experts-over-public.rationale: No stated position; Venizelos favoured technocratic reform yet the Venizelist base was mass-popular.

central-planning.rationale: Alien to its liberal-nationalist outlook; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Economic nationalism was not defined by the idea; no consistent doctrine.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Venizelos pursued state-led modernisation, but it was not a defining position of the idea.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Venizelos pursued land reform for small cultivators, inferred as a mild Venizelist leaning.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Incompatible with the bourgeois liberal nationalism of Venizelism.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not an issue for the idea; inferred rejection of radical monetary views.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Corporatism was not part of the idea; Venizelism was parliamentary-liberal.

one-party-rule.rationale: The idea was pursued through parliamentary and constitutional politics, and Venizelos fought a royalist-liberal electoral rivalry.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The idea began under King Otto and George I and most adherents supported a crowned Greek state, though the National Schism split Venizelists from the crown.

democracy-best.rationale: Kolettis demanded citizenship and constitutional rights for all Greeks, and Venizelism championed the 1911 constitution; democratic form was accepted rather than elevated.

direct-votes.rationale: Venizelism relied on parliamentary representation; direct democracy was not a theme.

workers-councils.rationale: Contrary to its liberal-nationalist, class-collaborationist framing.

right-to-secede.rationale: The idea is irredentist and unifying; it aims at the annexation of territories to Greece, not at regions leaving states.

natural-rulers.rationale: Not addressed; Greek nationalists claimed a civilisational mission but not a doctrine of natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Its history includes armed revolts, guerrilla action in Macedonia and a war for Asia Minor, so adherents did not hold violence unjustified.

war-builds-character.rationale: Greeks accepted war as the means to realise the idea, but the sources do not frame war as character-building; adherents split.

separate-church-state.rationale: Kolettis fused national and Orthodox identity, defining Greeks as Christians and linking the Church to the national cause.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Orthodoxy shaped national identity but the idea sought a constitutional state, not scriptural law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A national state with a strong army was the vehicle of the idea.

military-superiority.rationale: Venizelos reformed the army to win over rivals; the idea required Greek forces strong enough to prevail over neighbours.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Venizelos's memorandum argues for borders by Greek population majorities and proposes migrations so that remaining states are homogeneous, though Kolettis defined Greeks by religion.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The nation, not class, was the driving unit of the idea.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not part of the idea; inferred from its liberal orientation.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Anachronistic; Greek claims treated the land as historically Greek.

civilizational-union.rationale: The idea sought union of Greeks and Orthodox Christians, aiming to restore a Byzantine-style Orthodox centre.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The idea asks sacrifice for the nation, but it takes no stand on whether self-interest is moral.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Kolettis stressed the oath and the sacrifices of the struggle as national duties, yet he also insisted on civil rights for all Greeks, so it is mild.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred from nationalist wish to expand Greek demographic strength.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Anachronistic; the idea sought modernisation and state growth.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Nothing in the sources links the idea to a view on technological speed.

restore-past-order.rationale: The idea aimed to restore a Byzantine-style Orthodox empire centred on Constantinople, a lost order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Venizelos was pragmatic, but the idea itself is a doctrinal national programme; split.

direct-action.rationale: Politics ran through parliament and diplomacy as well as revolt; Venizelos used both, so action outside elections was not central.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources record no stance on whether methods should mirror intended ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Opposed to the state-building, civilizing aims of the idea.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not part of the idea; inferred rejection.

production-for-use.rationale: Not part of the idea; inferred.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Incompatible with its national-liberal programme; Venizelos opposed communism.

collective-farming.rationale: Venizelist agrarian policy favoured smallholders, not collectives.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Greek nationalism saw wars as national liberation, not a capitalist product.

taxation-theft.rationale: A state seeking war and expansion required taxation.

harm-principle.rationale: Not a theme of the idea.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The idea ascribes rights to the Hellenic nation as a collective that spans states, though Kolettis also stressed individual citizenship.

conscription.rationale: Venizelos reorganised and expanded compulsory military service and the Balkan Wars and Asia Minor campaign relied on mobilised conscripts.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The national project binds people to the state; exit as a check is alien.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is a national and sacred vehicle, not a business.

positive-liberty.rationale: The idea was about national liberation, and none of the sources discusses material preconditions of freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: No source ties the idea to a claim about media or university power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Kolettis used 'race' but defined Greeks by faith and history; no hereditarian claim.

organic-representation.rationale: Parliamentary representation, not organic corporatism, was the Venizelist framework.

total-state.rationale: A national liberal constitutional state is the vehicle; no ideology of directing every area of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Kolettis's speech presents Greece as a nation rising again after antiquity and Byzantium, completing a restoration.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Annexing Greek-populated and historically Greek lands is the defining aim of the idea.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Modern constitutional nationalism rejects lordly oaths as a basis for rule.

bound-labor.rationale: Rejected by a modern liberal state.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a classical-rationalist heritage.

universal-morality.rationale: Kolettis appeals to Hellenic heritage and Christianity, but no universal-moral doctrine is stated.

single-common-good.rationale: Kolettis stressed national unity over factional disputes, yet adherents were split along party lines.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Kolettis argued that Greeks born outside the kingdom held rights to citizenship in it, and the project aimed to gather diaspora Greeks into the state.

revive-national-language.rationale: Greek was already spoken; the question matches only loosely, since the Hellenic revival emphasised educated Greek language as a national tie.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Company governance was outside the idea, so adherents had no shared view.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education policy appears only as Hellenic cultural revival, not as a funding scheme.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal doctrine was no part of the idea; war finance was driven by national aims.

economic-freedom.rationale: The idea made no claim about economic and political freedom lasting together.

rule-by-example.rationale: The sources show no doctrine that rulers' moral example should replace law.

national-self-determination.rationale: Venizelos explicitly appealed to the nation's right to self-determination and the Allies' defence of small nations.

force-without-un.rationale: Greece went to war in Anatolia on its own after the Allies stalled; the UN did not exist, so inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Kolettis invoked faith and religion as the national bond, not reason alone.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Anachronistic for the period; the idea had no welfare-eligibility position.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Anachronistic; the kingdom and the idea had no welfare system to condition.

class-collaboration.rationale: Venizelism sought national unity across classes and treated nationalism as superior to class conflict.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The idea draws legitimacy from classical and Byzantine heritage that Kolettis celebrates.

dominated-front.rationale: The idea instead sought alignment with the Western powers and Britain, so no common front.

workers-nation.rationale: The idea treated workers as part of the Greek nation, rejecting class internationalism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred from the social conservatism of the period.

ban-interest.rationale: Not an Orthodox-Greek national position; inferred from a capitalist liberal outlook.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Greek claims were framed around nation and religion, not racial segregation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The state was seen as a national instrument, not a class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is anachronistic to a 19th and early 20th-century irredentist idea.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Nationalist state-building favoured homogenising citizens, and Venizelos wanted remaining states to be nationally uniform; inferred for immigrants.

elite-replacement.rationale: No such conspiracy theory belongs to the idea.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not part of the idea; no position is documented.

national-mission.rationale: Kolettis frames Greece as a successor to Athens that enlightened others and restoring a Byzantine centre, a civilising role, though not through imposing a form of government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred from traditional gender order of the time.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Kolettis's era was marked by patronage and Venizelists attacked royalist politicians, but it is not the idea's content.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Anachronistic; Orthodox identity would reject it.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from the army's central role.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The idea requires an active, expansionist and military state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Kolettis defined Greekness by religion and allegiance rather than blood.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Kolettis argued that all Greeks, born inside or outside the kingdom, should have equal civil rights, though the claim was limited to the Hellenic nation.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Socialist strategy is unrelated to the idea.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Greek claims relied on historical presence.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Religion-based civil law was Ottoman practice, but the idea took no stated stand on a uniform code.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Orthodox identity was national, but no law restricting conversion is documented as part of the idea.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Orthodox education was integral to Greek national schooling.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The statement concerns a socialist state, which does not apply to the idea.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Venizelos grounded claims in the self-determination of populations and Kolettis in the oath and participation of the Greek people.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade balance was not part of the idea's programme.

population-transfer.rationale: Venizelos proposed reciprocal migrations to make Turkey nearly entirely Muslim and later led the compulsory 1923 exchange.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Irredentist war was an accepted instrument.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The sources give no claim that struggle between peoples drives progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: No source records a view on outlawing anti-constitutional parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Anti-Ottoman struggle was against servitude, but the statement concerns republican theory.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutionalism was central to 1844 and 1911 politics, so separation of powers is plausible but not a stated aim.

vanguard-party.rationale: Opposed to a revolutionary-class party doctrine.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The idea did not prioritise the poor; its focus was national unification.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing is anachronistic to the idea.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labour-law detail was outside the idea and adherents shared no line.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The idea has no theory of the causes of poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Venizelos wanted homogeneity in the post-war settlement, inferred as a preference for ethnic and religious uniformity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not part of modern Greek constitutional practice.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls were not part of the programme and adherents were not united on them.

party-controls-media.rationale: Venizelism was a parliamentary liberal movement.

party-commands-army.rationale: Greek civil politics saw army under the crown and state.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Kolettis wanted citizenship for Greeks born abroad quickly; the question concerns foreign immigrants.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: No source links the idea to the pay of representatives.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Internal party discipline was not part of the idea; Greek parties were personal followings.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Greek nationalists sought a sovereign enlarged state, not supranational union.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The crown commanded the army, and the monarchy-versus-Venizelist split concerned who controlled it; split.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The idea ties national identity to the Great Church of Constantinople and the episcopal Orthodox hierarchy.

clerical-rule.rationale: Kolettis honoured the metropolitans of 1821 but the state was a constitutional kingdom, not clerical rule.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The idea is nationalist and mobilised its adherents for war.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Censorship for virtue is not documented as part of the idea.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Presidential term limits were irrelevant to a monarchy-era idea.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of officials was not part of the idea.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Greece pursued alliance with the Entente to realise its aims.

people-in-arms.rationale: Venizelos built a professional conscript army, not an armed militia.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The sources show no preference for rural over urban life; the idea centred on Athens and Constantinople.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Gathering Greeks divided between Greece and the Ottoman Empire is the central aim.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Hellenic education was prized in Kolettis's speech.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Kolettis assigned Greece a civilising role as heir to Athens and Byzantium.

death-penalty.rationale: Capital punishment was not an issue in the idea and adherents had no shared line.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from conservative Orthodox setting.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Anachronistic debate for the idea, which has no stated view on evolution teaching.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Censorship of pornography was not a theme of the idea.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Kolettis argued that those of Greek descent and 1821 fighters born abroad were entitled to citizenship.

minority-language-support.rationale: Venizelos aimed at national homogeneity; inferred as little support for minority-language rights.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The idea has no stated position on conformity and individuality.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Greece itself was a debtor state, but the idea took no stand on cancelling poor countries' debts.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Independence meant territorial union; economic transformation was not central.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The 1843 revolution forced an elected National Assembly, whose constitution Kolettis debated, and Venizelos revised the constitution in 1911.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The idea sought territory, not rapid economic growth, so it has no stated stance.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Global aid duties are anachronistic to the idea.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic; the idea predates nuclear weapons.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Monarchy vs republic split; no clear position.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions were not part of the idea.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Claims on historically Greek land were not traded away; the idea sought land, not to cede it, though Venizelos accepted compromise in 1930.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The idea took no doctrinal stand on the justification of property.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Soviet debate is unrelated to the idea.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed by the 19th-century Greek national project; adherents have no common line.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred: Greek governments pursued the programme through great-power and Entente alliances, though collective defence was not formulated.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred: the idea held that Greek lands taken without Greek consent should be redeemed, which applies the same logic to annexation.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Adherents split: Orthodoxy was central to the idea, yet the Greek state kept the church under civil control.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Adherents split: the crown versus Venizelos conflict in the National Schism showed no agreed role for the head of state.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred: the project was one of nation-state building by force of arms, so keeping national territory by force fits.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not addressed; Venizelos proposed self-determination and local arrangements in some regions, but the aim was union in one state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Inferred: Kolettis and Venizelos worked within a constitutional monarchy, not a sacred one, despite Byzantine memory.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed by the programme; adherents had no common line.

character-from-environment.rationale: Not addressed by the programme; adherents split.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred: the 1844 constitution that Kolettis defended and the 1911 Venizelist revision set rulers under constitutional law.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic: the programme predates the space age; no inference is possible.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Inferred: the 1844 constitution blended crown, senate and elected chamber, though the idea does not address constitutional design.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred: Greek parliamentary constitutionalism treated leaders as officeholders, though Venizelos drew mass devotion.

equal-parenting.rationale: Anachronistic: no relevant position is documented; adherents split.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The programme predates Marxism and was a nationalist, cross-class project; an adherent would reject class struggle. Anachronistic, so inferred.

land-redistribution.rationale: Venizelos, the programme's leading champion, pursued agrarian reform against large Thessalian estates; inferred as an adherent view.

refugee-return.rationale: The programme sought to bring Greeks into one state, so expelled Greeks returning is consistent, but the 1923 exchange was accepted in practice.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The programme exists to claim lands outside the kingdom because Greeks live there, as Kolettis and the 1919 memorandum argue.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Orthodox Greeks objected to Ottoman apostasy rules against their own flock; inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not addressed by the programme; Orthodox Greek society had no such dress law and would not seek one. Inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Anachronistic: no currency union was conceived in the period.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Uniting Greeks in the Ottoman Empire and elsewhere with the kingdom is the programme itself.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The programme wanted a Greek state, not autonomy for Greeks within the Ottoman state.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: It urged unification in a Greek state rather than a struggle for equal rights within the Ottoman Empire.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The programme appealed to history, religion and national memory rather than a materialist account; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not addressed; constitutional questions beyond the 1844 constitution are not part of the programme.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Women were excluded from politics in the period and the programme says nothing on parity; inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Not addressed; Venizelist Greece was trade-oriented but not autarkic.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Anachronistic: binding trade standards were not conceived in the period, so this is neutral.

moral-incentives.rationale: Nationalist mobilisation stressed duty to the nation, but the programme did not address work incentives. Inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Irregular bands and expeditions were used in pursuit of the programme, e.g. in Macedonia and Crete; inferred.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Not addressed; the kingdom had a monarchy but few titled hereditary classes.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Kolettis grounded the national idea in the Hellenic heritage and the Byzantine past, so history centred on Greece fits.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred: Venizelos framed Greek claims as liberating Hellenes, with a civilizing role in the East, rather than ruling others as such.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred from a nationalist programme that spread Greek education and identity through the unredeemed lands.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Anachronistic; the Megali Idea had no position on race-conscious policy.

public-money-creation.rationale: Anachronistic; monetary design was not part of the programme and adherents had no shared view.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Not addressed; Venizelist liberals and others had no shared view on capitalism's fate.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Reviving Byzantine and Ottoman-era Greek lands under Greek influence was the core aim.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred: Venizelist Greece sought integration with the Entente powers and the world economy rather than withdrawal.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred: a cross-class national programme with no Marxist class analysis.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred: the idea tied citizenship to nation and religion and had no doctrine of private discrimination; low confidence.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Venizelos's 1911 constitutional revision strengthened guaranteed rights in a modern constitutional state.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred: Greek nationalists contested the settlements by which the Great Powers left Greeks outside the kingdom.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred: royalist and Venizelist factions disagreed on monarchy.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred: liberal Greek nationalism favoured majority rule in Parliament.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred: the 1843 revolution forced a constitution on King Otto.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred: the 1844 Constitution and Venizelist liberalism made Parliament central.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred: mainstream nineteenth-century liberal opinion; not a Megali Idea matter.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred: nineteenth-century Greek farming; no principled view.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Inferred: the Idea demanded active national politics.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: anachronistic; liberal nationalism did not hold this theory.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred: Venizelist Greece sought integration with the Western capitalist order.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred: the Idea aimed to unite Greeks born outside the kingdom with those inside.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred: Venizelos relied on Allied support and foreign loans.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Recovering Greek-populated lands outside the kingdom was the Idea's core aim.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred: the Idea claimed Greek nation as heir to older Hellenic and Byzantine peoples among others.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred: Greek liberal nationalism sympathised with the Union side.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred: the Idea drew on historic symbols of Athens and Byzantium.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred: the Idea aimed at a European-style constitutional state.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred: the 1909 Goudi coup brought Venizelos to power and the army shaped politics.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred: traditional family structure of the era.

filial-duty.rationale: Orthodox Greek tradition honours family and elders; inferred, as the programme does not address it.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not addressed by the programme; no settled view.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The programme did not address foreign ownership; adherents would be split between nationalism and Venizelist liberal economics.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Orthodox social conservatism of the period lean against easy divorce; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Kolettis and Venizelos worked through parliamentary and party politics, not instructed delegates; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not addressed; no pension systems of this kind existed in the period.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The nineteenth-century Greek state rested on private smallholding; communal tenure is inferred to be rejected.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The 1844 and 1911 constitutions (see Venizelos) established parliamentary government with parliament's control of the budget; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Kolettis tied the nation to Greek language and heritage; making Greek the common public language is inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; adherents unlikely to have a settled view.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anachronistic; the programme's self-determination argument concerns nations, not group outcomes, so rejection is inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The programme aimed to redeem Greeks under Ottoman rule and irregular support to unredeemed regions fits it; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The 1919 case rested on national self-determination, so forcible intervention against allies is inferred to be rejected.

corporate-influence.rationale: Pre-1922 Greek nationalism had no programme on lobbying or campaign money; it was not an issue for the movement.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist aim of a sovereign Greek state, which would not welcome foreign-funded influence over Greek opinion.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from the nation-building aim of a larger Greek population; the sources do not state a population policy.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist wish to keep Greek land in Greek hands; the sources do not address property purchases.

job-guarantee.rationale: The movement had no employment programme; adherents were united by the territorial aim, not by economic policy.

democratic-peace.rationale: Venizelos appealed to the liberal Allied powers, but the idea was about national unification, not about democracy as a cause of peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred from a state-building nationalism that demanded citizens' loyalty and sacrifice, including an oath, for the national cause.

non-intervention.rationale: The programme itself meant acting beyond Greece's borders on behalf of Greeks in Ottoman lands and relied on great-power backing at Paris.

industrial-unions.rationale: Industrial relations were not part of the programme and adherents had no shared view.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Mainstream Venizelist nationalism rested on civic and religious inclusion of Greeks, not on a hidden-minority conspiracy theory; inferred, as the sources do not address it.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the idea's close tie to the Orthodox Church and a religiously defined Greek nation, which kept marriage a church matter.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Open-government rights were not an issue in this period and adherents had no shared view.

local-production.rationale: Not addressed; the programme concerned territory and nationhood, not the scale of production.

informal-organisation.rationale: Inferred from a state-led project run through the army, government and diplomacy, not through small informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred from the stress on Greek national sovereignty, though Venizelos also sought the Allied powers' treaties to secure Greek claims.

religious-nation.rationale: Kolettis's speech tied the Greek nation to Orthodox Christianity and Hellenic heritage, and the Ottoman millet system already sorted Greeks by religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from the aim of a sovereign Greek state with its own claims; Venizelos argued from national self-determination, not deference to a patron power.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from the centralised unitary Greek state the programme sought to extend over new regions, which pooled revenue nationally.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred from Venizelist liberalism, which kept private property and had no common-ownership programme.

defeat-communism.rationale: Anachronistic: the programme ended in 1922, but Venizelist liberals and royalists were both anti-communist; inferred from that.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred from Venizelist liberalism, which favoured modest reform without state monopoly of services.

religion-illusion.rationale: Kolettis defined Greeks by Orthodox faith and the idea drew on the Orthodox Byzantine Empire, so religion was treated as an enduring national pillar.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred from the Venizelist modernising, market-friendly liberalism; the programme itself did not address it.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the conservative social outlook of the period; the programme did not address gender.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from the family-centred social order of 19th and early 20th century Greece; not addressed by the programme.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred from the language purism (katharevousa) common in Greek nationalism of the period; not a stated tenet of the programme.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from Venizelos's argument at Paris for minority protection and binding treaties as the basis of settlement.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred: the programme sought a centralised nation-state, the opposite of communal self-governing cooperatives.

majority-settlement.rationale: Venizelos proposed reciprocal migrations to make populations match borders, and state resettlement of refugees followed.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Inferred: Venizelist liberals backed capitalism and rejected communism, and the programme did not seek a third way.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Kolettis grounded the idea in Hellenic and Byzantine heritage and the claim to lands where Greeks lived, over the claims of the current Ottoman rulers.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Anachronistic to the period; inferred that adherents accept the established history.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Anachronistic; not addressed in the sources, and no distinct adherent position.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Inferred: Venizelist liberal constitutionalism, though the National Schism saw harsh treatment of rivals.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred: Kolettis made Orthodoxy part of Greek identity, and the era's Greek state favoured the established church over proselytism.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred: the idea was about liberating Greeks, not exploiting overseas territories.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: a Muslim doctrine; the programme targeted Ottoman rule, not Islam as such.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: Venizelos's 1911 constitution made Greece a liberal constitutional state, though the Orthodox church was close to the state.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Anachronistic; not addressed in the sources.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Anachronistic; the idea sets the nation first, not intersecting oppressions.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the era's conservative social norms.

assisted-dying.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the era's Orthodox social norms.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Venizelism combined liberal and nationalist elements; the idea predates the modern left-right framing.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: liberal-capitalist Venizelism rejects Marxian alienation theory.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Anachronistic; Venizelos accepted minority protections and reciprocal exchanges rather than a culture-clash doctrine.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Kolettis spoke for the Orthodox faith and Hellenic heritage, while the constitution rested on the nation; adherents blend both.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred: Orthodoxy was central to Greek identity in the idea, so state neutrality in dress is unlikely to be favoured.

social-market-economy.rationale: Inferred: Venizelist liberalism favoured modest social reform within a market economy.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The idea required a strong army, and Venizelos reformed the Greek army to pursue the 1919-1922 campaign.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred: the idea was a state-led national project rather than a step-by-step growth doctrine.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Venizelos tied Greece to the Entente powers to win territory at the Paris Peace Conference, so staying out of blocs contradicted the strategy.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Greece was a monarchy throughout the Megali Idea's life and Kolettis served King Otto; adherents took hereditary kingship as normal, though Venizelist liberals made it constitutional.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Nineteenth-century Greek nationalism had no mutual-credit programme; inferred that adherents accepted ordinary banking.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Anachronistic; Venizelos relied on foreign loans and alliances, so inferred that adherents did not reject lender conditions.

property-franchise.rationale: The 1844 constitution gave wide male suffrage and Venizelism extended liberal citizenship; inferred that adherents did not tie the vote to wealth.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Anachronistic; ecofeminism is absent from this nineteenth-century nationalism, so inferred disagreement.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept alien to Greek liberal nationalism of the period; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Venizelist liberalism treated press and assembly freedoms as real constitutional rights; inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The 1843 revolution won a constitution and Venizelos's 1911 revision strengthened constitutional government and rule of law.

racial-franchise.rationale: Kolettis tied Greek citizenship to Orthodox Greek identity and heritage (s2) while Venizelos's programme offered minority protections (s3), so adherents are split on an ethnic franchise.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on it and no inference from principles settles it.

open-government-data.rationale: Venizelist liberal constitutionalism favoured public, parliamentary government; weak inference for open records.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The Orthodox Church was central to the national idea, so inferred that adherents accepted limits on marriage across faiths.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Venizelos proposed protected minorities and orderly exchanges (s3, s4); inferred that adherents did not endorse shop boycotts.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The idea was carried by kings, statesmen like Kolettis and Venizelos, and elected assemblies; sortition is inferred to be foreign to it.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The idea fused the nation with Orthodox Christianity and the Byzantine inheritance, so adherents would keep inherited doctrine; inferred from that fusion.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Megali Idea was a territorial programme with no economic doctrine; Venizelist liberalism and royalist conservatism differed, so no clear lean is inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Pre-1922 Greek nationalism assumed a conventional Orthodox society and the question is anachronistic; inferred as mildly opposed.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Kolettis's speech tied Hellenism to Orthodox Christianity and the Byzantine heritage, so state promotion of unbelief is contrary to the idea.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: A nation-building state with an army and gendarmerie, as Venizelos's reforms show, would not think of abolishing police and prisons; inferred.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The idea sought a unitary Greek state ruling over mixed populations, and Venizelos proposed population exchange rather than shared power; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The Orthodox Church had a large charitable role, but the idea had no welfare doctrine and Venizelist reform leaned to the state; split and inferred.

term-limits.rationale: The question is anachronistic for the 1844 to 1922 programme, and no source ties the idea to term limits; neutral is inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Kolettis and Venizelos worked in a representative parliamentary monarchy; delegable voting is anachronistic and inferred as foreign to it.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The idea predates the concept of extinction risk and says nothing about it; neutral is inferred.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The Orthodox Church, central to the idea's Hellenic-Christian identity, reserves priesthood to men and the movement's adherents accepted this.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Greek family law of the period gave the husband authority and Venizelist reform did not change it; inferred from the era.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from a citizenship-based irredentist nation-state programme that sought to unite Greeks, not to extend the franchise to foreigners.

rent-control.rationale: Housing policy was outside the programme; inferred as no stance.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the 19th-century liberal constitutional kingdom, which protected property and had no notion of abolishing patents or copyright.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from the parliamentary, constitutional character of the programme; drilled national youth movements belong to later authoritarian regimes outside the scope.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic: the programme ended in 1922, so nothing can be stated about nuclear weapons.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred: adherents wanted full sovereignty, but Venizelos relied on Entente great-power backing and Allied forces, so no clear stance.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Venizelos's 1919 memorandum stressed Ottoman persecution of Greeks, so adherents would have supported naming such killings; inferred, as the term is later.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Economic distribution was not part of the programme; inferred as no stance.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: the programme was pursued through war and armed liberation, so a committed adherent would reject absolute pacifism.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The programme joined the memory of classical Athens with the Byzantine Empire, presenting modern Greeks as the same nation as their ancient and medieval forebears.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from the 19th-century nationalist worldview, which treated sex as natural rather than constructed.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred: the programme predates feminist theory and treated women, if at all, as one traditional group.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from the Orthodox and nationalist veneration of the war dead and the Byzantine martyr-emperor tradition.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred: the programme was a constitutional nationalist project led by liberal politicians, though it drew on Orthodox imagery.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The programme aimed to gather the Greeks of the Ottoman Empire into one state centred on Constantinople, not to leave them in a diaspora.

culture-before-state.rationale: Kolettis presented the kingdom as the centre from which the state would redeem the unliberated Greeks, so state-building led.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from the traditional Orthodox setting of 19th-century Greek nationalism.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from the Orthodox setting, which treated tradition as authoritative.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred: the programme aimed at a Greek-led state, and the population exchange shows homogenising aims, but economic roles were not a stated principle.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred: Venizelos's memorandum sought to join regions with Greek populations into one Greek state.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred: the programme predates organised labour politics in Greece and does not address it.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred: a nation-building programme that subordinates class questions to national unity.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred: nineteenth-century Greek constitutions included a Senate; the programme is indifferent but the liberal-monarchist state was bicameral at times.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred: a national-state programme with no communal ownership aims.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred: the programme aims at a centralised nation-state around Constantinople.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from state-building nationalism favouring state control of money.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred: the programme puts the nation's destiny above individual interests.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The programme joins the Orthodox Byzantine memory to the national idea.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred: a centralised national state treats regional powers as grants from the centre.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The programme defines the nation by culture, language and faith, not race, though adherents spoke of the Greek 'race'.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in Hellenic descent and the classical heritage is central to the idea.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The programme aimed at expanding the state through war, culminating in the 1919-1922 Asia Minor campaign.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Kolettis's Hellenic heritage and Venizelos's claims joined Greeks across state borders, but the programme defined Greekness by Orthodoxy and descent as much as language alone.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from the programme's single constitutional Greek nation with equal citizenship; the Ottoman millet system it sought to replace is the nearest analogue.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred: Greek nationalists blamed great-power meddling for setbacks, yet relied on the powers' backing, so adherents were split on foreign plots.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred: the Megali Idea treated the University of Athens and Greek schools as instruments of Hellenic education, but it had no tuition policy.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Anachronistic: the programme never addressed pollution or resource taxes, and nothing in it implies a side.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred: the programme's appeal to the Hellenic heritage and the nation's destiny implies duties across generations, but it never spoke of the environment.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred from the period's Greek politics, where women lacked the vote and nationalism stressed martial and male national duties.

arms-reduction.rationale: The programme was pursued through army build-up and war, culminating in the 1919-1922 campaign, so adherents did not favor minimal armaments.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Venizelos argued Greece's case openly at the Paris Peace Conference, but Greek aims were also pursued through secret wartime commitments, so the programme did not settle this.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred: Venizelist liberalism favored open commerce and foreign loans for development, and capital controls were not part of the programme.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from the irredentist programme's reliance on the Greek army and the state's armed forces; irregular bands were also used.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The Megali Idea relied on conscription and the army to carry out national aims, so soldiers refusing to fight is against it.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Venizelos passed early labour laws, but collective bargaining was no part of the national project.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Anachronistic; the programme ended in 1922 with no view on tax credits.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Anachronistic; the programme had no view on legal borrowing limits and the war was funded by debt.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred: the programme was about territory and the Greek state's standing, not reworking international economic rules.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The programme sought to extend the constitutional kingdom, not smash it; Venizelos reformed the state and army from within.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred from the programme's single national state centred on Constantinople, which leaves no space for communities choosing separate systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Anachronistic; the sources do not discuss it.

sacred-nation.rationale: Kolettis's 1844 speech joins the Hellenic heritage, Orthodoxy and the oath of the nation, which gives the Greek nation a lasting sacred standing.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Anachronistic; the programme had no view on student loans.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: Venizelist Greece saw itself as a nation uniting its parts, not as a core exploiting regions; the claim was about Greeks outside the kingdom.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from the programme's Hellenic and Orthodox heritage, which treats a shared human character as the base of the nation.

missingStatements.text: Greeks and other Christians living under foreign rule should be liberated and joined to their own national state.
missingStatements.rationale: Kolettis called on the deputies to remember the freedom owed to all Christians and Hellenes outside the kingdom, the core of the idea.

missingStatements.text: Constantinople should be the capital of a state that unites its nation.
missingStatements.rationale: Kolettis named Constantinople the great capital and hope of Hellenism; the idea aimed at a state centred there.
missingStatements.declined: Too specific to one city and one national project; other ideologies cannot take a side on it.

notes: Venizelist and royalist adherents differed on monarchy, war aims in 1914-17 and the Asia Minor campaign; Kolettis defined Greeks by Orthodox faith while Venizelos argued from population majorities. Many economic and social answers are inferred.
